# MM-P2-L3-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Machining induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-IH03

Scope
- This document provides preventive and corrective maintenance instructions for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) located on line P2-L3. It covers mechanical, electrical and cooling system checks necessary to maintain reliable heating to the target billet temperature and safe operation of the induction coil system.
- This procedure supplements site-level quality and process requirements; follow QS-PROC-10 and SOP-P2-L3-02 for production interface and lockout/tagout. Refer to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for schematic and spare-parts mapping.

Background and rationale
- EQ-P2-L3-IH03 is a high-power induction heater used to bring billets to machining temperature. Proper maintenance reduces thermal non-uniformity, prevents coil damage, and avoids production rejects. The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C. Maintaining design cooling and electrical parameters is essential to achieve this target without overstressing components.
- The coil requires continuous cooling during operation. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. Operating below this flow risks rapid coil failure and compromised heating performance.

Tools
- Insulated hand tools suitable for electrical work.
- Flow indicator calibrator and inline flow meter compatible with the system.
- Thermal imaging camera or surface pyrometer for coil and housing inspection.
- Vibration meter and strobe light for rotation checks (if applicable to drive components).
- Multimeter and clamp ammeter rated for system voltages/currents.
- Torque tools only where factory torque specifications are provided in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.
- Personal protective equipment: arc-rated gloves, face shield, insulated boots, and hearing protection.

Procedure
Preparation
- Coordinate with production per SOP-P2-L3-02 before starting any maintenance. Ensure process owner signs off on billet flow and that replacement billets are not in the heater path.
- Apply lockout/tagout per QS-PROC-10 for electrical supply and water supply isolation. Verify zero energy state before opening panels.

Visual inspection
- Inspect the induction coil for signs of cracking, discoloration, or insulation breakdown. Use thermal imaging to identify hot spots when safe and permitted.
- Verify coil mounting hardware is secure per drawing in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3. Replace any fasteners or insulators that show damage.
- Inspect water connections, hoses, and quick-disconnect fittings for leakage, abrasion, and proper sealing. Check for scale or biofouling at visible joints and strainers.

Cooling system verification
- Confirm the cooling water supply system is delivering adequate flow and pressure to the heater. Use the inline flow meter to confirm that coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is achieved. If flow is below minimum, stop and trace to pump, filter, or valve issues.
- Clean strainers and filters according to the service schedule in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3. If deposits are found, collect samples and log condition in the maintenance record.

Electrical checks
- With power isolated and lockout in place, inspect power connections for looseness, corrosion, or overheating signs. Measure contact resistance where accessible and compare to historical records.
- Inspect and test protective interlocks and thermal cutouts. Verify wiring to control relays and sensors matches the schematic in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.
- After reassembly and removal of lockout/tagout, perform controlled power-up following SOP-P2-L3-02. Monitor for abnormal current or alarm conditions and be prepared to isolate system immediately.

Operational verification and tuning
- Bring the heater to operational state under supervision of process engineer. Monitor billet temperature feedback and compare to the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03): 1175 °C. Adjust tuning parameters only within limits provided in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 and in consultation with process engineering.
- If temperature cannot be achieved while coil cooling water flow remains at or above the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min, escalate to engineering for further diagnostic steps.

Examples and common fault modes
- Example: If the heater reaches setpoint intermittently and then falls away, check for intermittent loss of cooling flow, contaminated flow meter, or partial clogging of internal passages. Record instances and compare with pump operation logs.
- Example: Visible coil hot spot with normal flow suggests coil insulation breach or localized shorting; remove from service and tag for coil replacement per MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.

Records to keep
- Record of lockout/tagout authorization and completion per QS-PROC-10.
- Maintenance log entry with date, technician name, work performed, parts replaced (referenced by MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3), and measured cooling flow values. Include explicit statement when coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min is met or not met.
- Calibration certificates for flow meter and temperature sensors used during verification.
- Incident report and corrective action if target billet temperature is not achievable: include observed temperature, steps taken, and reference to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 diagnostics.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical and electrical integrity verified with no loose connections or coolant leaks present.
- Coil cooling water flow meets or exceeds the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min as measured at the heater inlet.
- Heater achieves and holds the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C under normal process load, with stable control signals and no protective trips.
- All work completed is recorded in the maintenance management system and referenced to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for parts and QS-PROC-10 for procedural adherence.
- If any acceptance criterion is not met, the heater shall remain tagged out and escalated per SOP-P2-L3-02 until corrective actions are implemented and re-verification is successful.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3
- QS-PROC-10
- SOP-P2-L3-02
